tasks.title: The website's PRD
tasks.text: write the PRD of the website this request describes (docs/product/prd.md), from the request and the documents the project holds (docs/brand/, docs/business/ and the like when they exist): who the audience is, the one action a visitor should take, the pages, what success is and what is out of scope. Ask the person what only they can answer; never invent an audience or a goal.

tasks.title: The website as a feature
tasks.text: the PRD is done (docs/product/prd.md). Specify the website the request describes as one feature, docs/product/specs/website.md: every page, section by section, with its goal and its content and copy requirements; the responsive widths 1280 and 375; light and dark; motion only to show a state, and reduced motion; accessibility; the performance budget.

tasks.title: Site map and visitor paths
tasks.text: the PRD and the feature specification are done (docs/product/prd.md and docs/product/specs/website.md). Define the site map, the page inventory with the regions and states of each page, and the visitor's paths from arrival to the one action, with the failure branches and the keyboard path: write docs/design/flows.md.

tasks.title: Visual foundations
tasks.text: the site map and the visitor's paths are done (docs/design/flows.md). Define the visual foundations the website is built from (colours with light and dark values, type, spacing, radii, elevation, grid and the components), from the brand documents the project holds (docs/brand/ when it exists; otherwise ask the person for the identity facts needed), and write the design system document in docs/design/, where the brief will read it.

tasks.title: One brief for the whole website
tasks.text: the design system and the site map are done (the design system document under docs/design/ and docs/design/flows.md), and so is the specification (docs/product/specs/website.md). Write one design brief for the whole website, docs/design/briefs/website.md: the creative direction, every page, all the copy, the animations, and for every claim how the page proves it. Take every text from a document or from the person; never write final copy of your own.

tasks.title: The brief as code prototypes
tasks.text: the design brief is done (docs/design/briefs/website.md). Run it in its code-prototype mode: one static HTML page for each page of the site, rendered to PNG at 1280 and 375 pixels wide, in light and in dark, with the results document docs/design/results/website.md. Ask the person which direction to keep.

tasks.title: Hand the mockups to engineering
tasks.text: the mockups are done and the person has chosen among them (docs/design/results/website.md and the pages under docs/design/results/website/). Hand the chosen mockups to engineering, one hand-off document for each page of the site, docs/design/handoff/<page>.md, with the exported HTML as its reference.

tasks.title: Build the site
tasks.text: the hand-offs are done (docs/design/handoff/). Build the website from them as a static site in the folder the request names (site/ when it names none), touching that folder only, so that each change set stays inside it. The hand-off documents and the specification (docs/product/specs/website.md) define the behaviour; the check that proves it is that every page of the hand-off exists in that folder and renders at 1280 and 375 pixels wide, in light and in dark, as its mockup does. Propose the commit and do not make it.
